title: Finite tensor-kernel tests detect factorization when the cokernel is finitely presented
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $U,V,W$ be $R$-modules, and $f:U\to V$ and $g:U\to W$ be $R$-linear maps. Suppose the quotient $V/f(U)$, namely the cokernel of $f$, is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. If for every finitely presented $R$-module $Q$ one has $\ker(f\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_Q)\subseteq\ker(g\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_Q)$ as submodules of $U\otimes_RQ$, then there is an $R$-linear map $h:V\to W$ with $g=h\circ f$. Tensor products and their induced maps are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No finite-generation, flatness or injectivity hypothesis on $U,V,W$ or $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 059D, lemma-domination, combined with Tag 059C, lemma-domination-fp: finite-presentation tests suffice for domination, and domination implies factorization when the cokernel of f is finitely presented.
